Goldman pitches $5.4B debt for Microsoft-tied data center



Goldman Sachs is testing investor demand for a roughly $5.4 billion debt package to fund a Blackstone-backed QTS data center tied to Microsoft.

The Details:

•	Deal structure: The proposed financing includes about $4.9 billion of secured bonds and roughly $500 million in a term loan.

•	Timing uncertainty: Exact timing is still being discussed after a recent selloff in AI-linked debt, and the plans may still change.

•	Market backdrop: The move comes as bubble concerns and higher risk premiums push up funding costs for AI infrastructure projects.

Qualcomm said its two near-term custom silicon wins will begin generating revenue in the December quarter, with wafer production underway and HBC Gen 1 taped out.

The Details:

•	Custom silicon timeline: The company has begun wafer production on custom silicon and completed the tape-out of HBC Gen 1, targeting initial shipments in the December quarter.

•	Automotive outlook: Qualcomm now expects annualized automotive sales of about $7 billion exiting fiscal 2026, with QCT automotive revenue growth of about 60% year over year in Q4.

•	Samsung position: Qualcomm said its position at Samsung remains strong, with Snapdragon powering about 70% of Samsung’s flagship devices.

Meta provides 2026 expense view, no 2027 CapEx guidance



Meta $META CFO Susan Li said the company is not giving specific 2027 CapEx guidance, calling infrastructure planning highly dynamic.

The Details:

•	CapEx outlook: Meta is focusing on maximizing capacity in 2026 and 2027, preserving flexibility to adjust server decisions for 2028 and beyond.

•	Expense guide: Full-year 2026 total expenses are now expected in the range of $165B–$169B.

•	Operating income: Excluding Q2 legal charges and severance, Q2 operating income would have risen 9% year over year.

•	Compute use: CEO Mark Zuckerberg said a substantial amount of compute is devoted to training models to remain a leading AI lab.

Bottom Line: Meta is prioritizing near-term capacity and flexibility, with 2026 expenses guided but 2027 CapEx left open.

Samsung Electronics Q2 2026 — Key Takeaways

Highlights:

•	Q2 Revenue: 171 trillion won (in line with company estimate)

•	Q2 Operating Profit: 89.4 trillion won (matched guidance)

•	Q2 Net Profit: 71.3 trillion won (beat LSEG estimate of 68.5T won)

Segment Performance:

•	Chip Division: 89.2 trillion won operating profit — strong server chip demand driving results

•	Display Unit: 700 billion won operating profit

•	Mobile Division: 700 billion won operating loss — facing demand slowdown

H2 2026 Outlook:

•	Server chips: Demand strength expected to continue

•	Mobile/PC chips: Demand slowdown anticipated

•	Chip supply: Shortage expected to persist through H2

•	Foundry business: Revenue projected to grow double-digits for the full year

•	Smartphones: Company aims to gain market share in H2
